title: Model Identity, Licensing, and Provenance
summary: Identify the exact model artifact, distinguish public weights from permissions and Open Source AI, and make a reviewable license and lineage decision before deployment.
objectives: Separate an AI system, model architecture, weights, derivative, quantization, runtime, and hosted product.
Create and verify an immutable identity record for the exact artifact proposed for deployment.
Evaluate license, acceptable-use, attribution, redistribution, and derivative evidence without treating availability or metadata as permission.
Record lineage, contradictions, evidence gaps, accountable reviewers, and a dated, expiring adoption decision.
Repair and test an offline policy gate that must hold rather than approve when required evidence is unknown or contradictory.

sections.title: Name the exact object under review
paragraphs: A provider name or model family is not a deployable identity. Separate the AI system from its architecture, weights, tokenizer, configuration, prompt or chat template, adapters, quantization, inference runtime, dependencies, and surrounding application. Each component can have a different publisher, version, license, security boundary, and failure mode.

Write the deployment object as an explicit tuple: publisher and repository, immutable revision, weight filename, byte count and SHA-256, base-model lineage and evidence status, derivative identity, quantization method and parameters, tokenizer digest, prompt-template revision, runtime name and version, hardware architecture, and deployment shape. If a required element is unresolved, promotion must stop or follow an authorized exception process.

code.label: Artifact identity tuple
code.code:
publisher/repository@immutable-revision
  weights: filename, byte count, SHA-256
  derivative: type, publisher, revision
  base: repository, revision, evidence status
  quantization: method, bits, group size in weights
  tokenizer: filename, SHA-256
  prompt template: identifier, revision
  runtime: name, version, hardware architecture
  deployment: shape, use, distribution, users

sections.title: Distinguish downloadable, open-weight, and Open Source AI claims
paragraphs: Downloadable or publicly accessible weights establish access under presented conditions. They do not by themselves establish permission for commercial use, modification, redistribution, hosting, every user group, or every field of use. They also do not prove provenance, safety, support, or reproducibility.

The Open Source Initiative's Open Source AI Definition version 1.0 requires freedoms to use, study, modify, and share, plus access to the preferred form for making modifications, including relevant data information, code, and parameters. Apply that label only after evaluating the definition. Otherwise use a narrower evidence label, such as publicly downloadable weights under named terms.

code.label: Evidence labels that must remain distinct
code.code:
PUBLICLY DOWNLOADABLE: retrieval was offered under presented conditions
NAMED TERMS: pinned controlling text was collected
PERMITTED USE: the exact use, distribution, and users were mapped
OPEN SOURCE AI: the OSI definition requirements were evaluated
LEGAL OR POLICY APPROVAL: an authorized human issued the decision

sections.title: Review all applicable terms as one decision
paragraphs: Collect the license at the immutable revision, repository terms, acceptable-use policy, model card, notices, attribution requirements, base-model and adapter terms, and relevant dataset obligations. Preserve the retrieved text, source, revision, and date. Hugging Face documents a model-card metadata license field for discovery, but metadata does not replace the applicable controlling text.

Map stated use, distribution, and users separately to permissions, obligations, restrictions, and unknowns. Each matrix row must repeat the corresponding proposed value, preventing an old permission row from silently approving a changed scope. The lab's controlling excerpts are fictional educational policy, not legal advice or real vendor grants. Consequential interpretation remains a human legal or policy responsibility.

code.label: Minimum bound terms matrix row
code.code:
{
  "dimension": "distribution",
  "proposedValue": "external-api",
  "status": "unknown",
  "evidenceStatus": "unknown",
  "source": "pinned controlling text does not cover this value"
}

sections.title: Trace lineage and preserve evidence gaps
paragraphs: Model cards can describe intended uses, limitations, datasets, training, base models, evaluations, licenses, and library compatibility. Treat these as claims to verify. Follow base-model, fine-tune, adapter, merge, conversion, quantization, and tokenizer links until the ancestry and material transformations of the proposed artifact are understood. The SPDX AI Profile can structure model and provenance data, but it does not automatically grant legal or policy approval.

A SHA-256 match shows that local bytes match the bytes named by a digest. It does not prove who trained the model, which data were used, whether a claimed base was used, or whether the publisher had authority to distribute it. The lab also confines reads to its artifacts directory after resolving symlinks. That protects this exercise's boundary, but neither containment nor a digest proves provenance.

code.label: Example provenance graph with unresolved evidence
code.code:
Fictional Base r1
  -> fine-tune claim: UNKNOWN EVIDENCE
Fictional Derivative r7
  -> quantization: fictional-int4, 4 bits, group size 128 weights
Synthetic local artifact
  -> weights digest: VERIFIED
  -> tokenizer digest: MISMATCH
Result: byte identity partly verified; claimed lineage not proved

sections.title: Issue a dated, expiring, and reversible decision
paragraphs: The adoption record identifies the exact artifact tuple, stated use, distribution, users, applicable terms, notices, lineage, evidence sources, unresolved gaps, reviewers, scope, decision date, expiry, and re-review triggers. Technical recommendation, security review, legal or policy interpretation, and operational acceptance remain separate authorities.

Use an explicit as-of date so the same input produces the same result without relying on the machine clock. Validate both dates as real Gregorian calendar dates. A decision is valid before its expiry date and expired on the expiry date. Re-review on expiry or whenever the artifact, terms, audience, distribution, use, tokenizer, template, runtime, derivative, or lineage changes.

code.label: Disposition vocabulary used in the lab
code.code:
approve-isolated-evaluation: fictional gate passed for the exact unexpired scope
hold-for-evidence: unknown, contradictory, mismatched, uncovered, or expired
reject: controlling fictional terms directly prohibit the stated scope
None of these values is legal approval.

sections.title: Apply one evidence method across provider families
paragraphs: For Meta Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral, Qwen, Phi, NVIDIA Nemotron, and Z.ai GLM, begin with the publisher and exact repository rather than a family nickname. Pin an immutable revision and record exact weight, tokenizer, configuration, template, adapter, and quantization files. Record the declared architecture with its source, plus the exact runtime name, version, hardware architecture, and deployment shape actually proposed.

For every family, retrieve controlling terms and notices from the pinned publisher source, then trace base and derivative links. Label each claim direct, inferred, unknown, or contradictory. This method does not assert a current license, architecture, permission, benchmark, price, or Open Source AI status for any listed family. Those conclusions require evidence for the exact selected artifact and revision.

code.label: Source-labelled provider review queue
code.code:
Meta Llama | collect exact publisher repository, revision, files, terms
DeepSeek | collect exact publisher repository, revision, files, terms
Mistral | collect exact publisher repository, revision, files, terms

Never transfer a license or architecture conclusion between revisions.

sections.title: Worked example: decide from a synthetic dossier
paragraphs: The supplied Atlas fixture is entirely synthetic. Its three-byte weights file contains abc, whose SHA-256 is ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad. Its empty tokenizer has SHA-256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855. The CLI computes these hashes from fixture bytes. All twelve required checks are known, all three matrix values match the proposed scope, and no provenance gap is recorded.

With as-of date 2026-09-20, the decision dated 2026-09-20 has not reached its 30-day expiry. Completeness is 12 of 12, or 100 percent, and the fictional disposition is approve-isolated-evaluation. This does not grant rights, validate a vendor license, prove training lineage, measure model quality, or authorize production.

sections.title: Run the offline identity and evidence gate lab
paragraphs: The public lab directory is https://github.com/project42dev/project42-content/tree/main/training/self-hosted-model-operations/model-identity-license-and-provenance/lab. From the repository root, run the commands below with Node.js 22. No dependency installation, network, GPU, model download, or remote artifact execution is needed. Numeric fixture values are synthetic; only hashes and decisions are derived from the returned files and code.

The starter has one bounded defect in decide: after preserving explicit rejection, it approves evidence problems instead of holding. Validation, proposal-to-matrix binding, calendar expiry, artifact containment, and independent tests are already complete. Edit only src/evaluate.mjs. The test runner gathers all cases and treats exceptions as failures. Attempt the repair before consulting the separate reference.

code.label: Commands from the repository root
code.code:
cd training/self-hosted-model-operations/model-identity-license-and-provenance/lab/
node src/cli.mjs fixtures/positive.json --as-of 2026-09-20
node test/run-tests.mjs starter
# edit only src/evaluate.mjs, then:
node test/run-tests.mjs learner
# after attempting the repair:
node test/run-tests.mjs reference

sections.title: Learner variation: changed scope, contradictions, and expiry
paragraphs: Evaluate changeduse.json after the worked example. Its bytes still match, but external API distribution is unknown, so the correct disposition is hold-for-evidence. Independent mutation tests also change proposed use, distribution, or users without changing the matrix. Correct validation rejects each stale matrix because every proposedValue must equal dossier.proposed[row.dimension].

The test suite also checks positive before expiry, on expiry, after expiry, invalid dates, digest and lineage gaps, explicit prohibition, traversal outside artifacts, and a symlink canary when the platform permits it. Repair only the decision priority: direct prohibition rejects; otherwise any missing check or problem holds; only a complete, unexpired, exact isolated-evaluation scope approves.

code.label: Required gate priority and worked answer

activity.title: Build an artifact identity and terms decision
instructions: Run the completed positive fixture and connect each output field to the artifact tuple, terms matrix, provenance graph, decision date, and as-of date.
Run the starter tests and confirm that all cases are gathered. Observe that only the deliberate decision-gate cases fail.
Inspect hold.json and changeduse.json. Identify the digest mismatch, contradiction, lineage gap, and changed distribution before changing code.
Edit only src/evaluate.mjs. Preserve the explicit reject rule, add a general hold gate for evidence problems, and do not edit validation, assessment, CLI, fixtures, tests, or expected outcomes.
Rerun learner tests. After making an attempt, compare the focused change with solution/repair.patch and run the independent reference suite.

For a real candidate, without downloading or executing remote artifacts, record publisher, repository, immutable revision, exact files, independently available digests, base lineage, derivative, tokenizer, template, runtime, architecture, intended use, distribution, users, decision date, expiry, and unresolved fields.
Retrieve controlling terms from the pinned authoritative source, map the exact proposed scope, label evidence status, and route legal or policy interpretation to an authorized human.
evidence: A verified model identity tuple containing immutable revisions, exact material files, digests, tokenizer, template, runtime, architecture, derivative, and base lineage.
A three-row terms matrix bound to the proposed use, distribution, and users, while separating metadata from controlling text.
A provenance graph that distinguishes byte verification from unproved lineage claims.
A focused evaluator repair for which positive, hold, reject, changed-scope, expiry, validation, and containment tests pass.
A dated disposition with deterministic as-of evaluation and artifact, terms, audience, distribution, use, and expiry triggers.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which missing, stale, or changed fact most affects the disposition, and why is holding for evidence more defensible than treating that fact as permission?

instructorScript.reducedMotionAlternative: Present the deployment tuple and lineage as static tables. Reveal no animated dependency lines; use numbered rows and textual status labels.

questions.prompt: Which record most precisely identifies a proposed model deployment?
choices: The model family nickname
The provider logo and parameter count
Publisher, repository, immutable revision, artifact digests, lineage, quantization, tokenizer, template, runtime, and architecture
The date someone first heard about the model
questions.explanation: A deployable identity must pin every material component and transformation, not only a family name.

questions.prompt: What does public availability of model weights prove by itself?
choices: Only that the weights are publicly obtainable under some presented conditions
That every commercial and redistribution use is allowed
That the complete AI system is Open Source
That the artifact is safe and supported
questions.explanation: Availability alone does not establish permissions, Open Source AI status, safety, provenance, or support.

questions.prompt: A repository metadata field names a common license, but pinned controlling text conflicts with it. What should the automated fictional policy gate do?
choices: Approve from the metadata label
Ignore the controlling text
Hold for evidence or reject if the exact scope is directly prohibited
Ask the runtime to choose a license
questions.explanation: Metadata is not controlling text. Contradiction prevents approval, while a directly evidenced prohibition supports rejection under the fictional gate.

questions.prompt: What does a matching SHA-256 digest establish?
choices: The local bytes match the bytes associated with that digest
The publisher trained the model as claimed
Every lineage statement is true
The artifact is legally approved
questions.explanation: A digest verifies byte identity. It does not prove origin, training data, lineage, authority, or legal approval.

questions.prompt: Who should resolve a consequential license ambiguity?
choices: The model being reviewed
Any learner who can download the file
An authorized legal or policy reviewer with the exact source and use context
The runtime automatically
questions.explanation: The lab structures evidence but cannot substitute for authorized legal or policy interpretation.

questions.prompt: Why must changeduse.json be held even though its artifact bytes match?
choices: Every matching digest requires rejection
Its external API distribution is not covered by directly evidenced fictional terms
The fixture has no runtime
Node.js cannot hash files
questions.explanation: A prior scope decision does not carry over to a changed distribution whose permission evidence is unknown.

questions.prompt: When a decision expires on 2026-10-20, which as-of date first requires re-review?
choices: Only when the machine clock changes
questions.explanation: The fictional policy treats the decision as expired on its calculated expiry date.
